age.evidence: Mice were 7 weeks of age when diet interventions began.

sex.evidence: Wild type male C57BL/6 J mice were obtained from the Monash Animal Research Platform (MARP; Clayton, VIC, Australia).

dosing.evidence: Psilocybin (USONA Institute Investigational Drug Supply Program; Lot# AMS0167) was dissolved in saline (Baxter Healthcare Pty Ltd, NSW, Australia) and administered at a dose of 1 mg/kg. ... All compounds were administered intraperitoneally using a 29 G needle in a volume of 5 mL/kg.

group_housing.evidence: 7-week-old mice were given access to HFD for 16-20 weeks to promote DIO ... and remained group-housed. ... One month prior to the psilocybin injection (designated day 0) all mice were single housed.

day_night_flipped.evidence: All mice were housed under a 12:12 light cycle (lights off at 1900h). ... All compounds were administered during the inactive phase typically between 1100-1300 h.

enrichment_housing.evidence: Sawdust and tissue paper nesting material were provided throughout.

assays.assay_description: Daily manual measurement of food (HFD or low-fat Chow) intake in single-housed DIO male mice (home cages and TSE PhenoMaster metabolic cages) from day -8 through a 28-day diet intervention following a single i.p. injection of psilocybin (1 mg/kg) or saline; food intake converted to energy intake, energy intake normalised to body weight, post-injection intake as % of pre-injection, and feeding efficiency. Body weight and indirect calorimetry (VO2, CO2, RER, energy expenditure) are physiological and not scored.

application_type.evidence: All compounds were administered intraperitoneally using a 29 G needle in a volume of 5 mL/kg.

setup_habituation.evidence: For the next 24 days, body weights and food intake were measured three times per week as the mice acclimatised to single housing. ... Mice were habituated to indirect calorimetry / metabolic cages for 10 days from day -18 to -9.

setup_restrain.evidence: Food intake measured in home/metabolic cages with food and water ad libitum; no restraint described during monitoring.

food_restriction.evidence: Rodent food (high-fat diet (HFD) or Chow - see details below) and water were available ad libitum.

water_restriction.evidence: Rodent food (high-fat diet (HFD) or Chow - see details below) and water were available ad libitum.

time_to_assay.evidence: From day -8 onwards, body weight and food intake were measured daily. ... On day 0, all mice received an injection ... Mice were maintained on their respective diets for 28 days and body weight and food intake were measured daily.

sample_size.evidence: HFD-SAL n = 14; HFD-PSI: n = 15; Chow-SAL: n = 15; Chow-PSI: n = 16; Resistant: n = 23; Susceptible: n = 8.

outcomes.summary: A single 1 mg/kg dose of psilocybin did not alter HFD food or energy intake in DIO mice, and had no overall effect on food/energy intake in mice switched to Chow. However, weight-loss-susceptible Chow mice (7 of 8 psilocybin-treated) showed significantly reduced food and energy intake, reduced feeding efficiency, and reduced post-injection intake relative to baseline compared with resistant mice.
outcomes.statistics: Susceptible vs resistant: food and energy intake p = 0.0025; feeding efficiency p < 0.0001 (Student's t-test). Psilocybin overall effect on Chow food/energy intake not significant (Supplementary Tables 8, 9).
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin had no overall effect on food and energy intake for Chow mice throughout the diet intervention period (Fig. 3G, H, J, K; Supplementary Table 8, 9). Despite no overall impact on food intake, weight loss susceptible mice (7 of 8 treated with psilocybin) had significantly reduced food and energy intake (p = 0.0025; Fig. 3I, L), and a reduced feeding efficiency (p < 0.0001; Fig. 3N).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Reported measures: cumulative/total food intake, energy intake, energy intake normalised to daily body weight, post-injection energy intake as a percentage of pre-injection, and feeding efficiency (Figs. 3G-N, 4A-J).

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Food intake was manually measured once per day; daily totals compared across days, no within-session binning.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No meal pattern, bout or transition analysis reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Food intake quantified only as grams/energy consumed by weighing; no ethological acts scored.

B5_social.evidence: Mice single housed; no social construct targeted.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Body weight and food intake were manually measured once per day during indirect calorimetry assessments.

B8_multivariate.evidence: Only univariate tests (multiple linear regression, two-way ANOVA, t-tests) reported.

E1_environment_type.evidence: One month prior to the psilocybin injection (designated day 0) all mice were single housed. ... body weight and food intake were measured daily.

E3_bedding.evidence: Sawdust and tissue paper nesting material were provided throughout.

E4_nesting.evidence: Sawdust and tissue paper nesting material were provided throughout.

E6_spatial.evidence: Single home/metabolic cage; no compartments described.

E7_social_context.evidence: Certain cohorts of mice were all single housed during diet interventions to obtain accurate food intake measurements.

E8_food_water.evidence: Rodent food (high-fat diet (HFD) or Chow - see details below) and water were available ad libitum.

D1_continuity.evidence: From day -8 onwards, body weight and food intake were measured daily ... maintained on their respective diets for 28 days and body weight and food intake were measured daily (24-h cumulative intake in home cage).

D2_session_duration.evidence: Daily food intake reflects 24-h accumulation; 24 h PhenoMaster recordings were performed.

D3_recording_days.evidence: From day -8 onwards, body weight and food intake were measured daily ... for 28 days.

D4_baseline.evidence: Food intake was measured daily prior to and beyond the drug and diet interventions; average energy intake compared pre- and post-psilocybin injection (Fig. 4).

D5_followup.evidence: Mice were maintained on their respective diets for 28 days and body weight and food intake were measured daily.

D6_circadian.evidence: Daily (24 h) food intake measurements and 24 h PhenoMaster recordings.

judge_notes: Two of three candidates (deepseek4, gemma4) identified a food-intake monitoring assay; qwen returned no assays. Included one assay since food intake is a behavioural (ingestive) outcome explicitly framed as 'feeding behaviour'.
Body weight and indirect calorimetry (VO2, CO2, RER, energy expenditure) excluded as purely physiological; IHC excluded as ex vivo.
B1 set to 4-6 (score 2): food intake, energy intake, BW-normalised energy intake, % baseline intake, feeding efficiency; gemma's score 2 with '2-3' label was internally inconsistent.
B4 scored 0: intake quantified by weighing food rather than scoring discrete ethological acts.
D1/D2/D6 follow deepseek4 (continuous 24-h home-cage intake), medium confidence, because intake was measured as 24-h accumulation with food continuously available.
day_night_flipped set to 'no': lights off at 1900 h and dosing during inactive phase (1100-1300 h) indicates a standard cycle.
group_housing 'no' reflects single housing during the testing period; mice were group-housed during the DIO phase.
Sample size taken from Fig. 3/4 single-housed cohort (n=60); weight-change analyses used larger pooled cohorts.
